parsed.notes: Lens B only. I did not raise support, quote-fidelity, or pincite defects. Across disclosed treatment edges, all case-edge entries were field_iii='mentioned'; the only substantive currency issues found were Trupiano's unverified treatment/progeny record and Chadwick's caution/Acevedo limitation.

reasons: Virginia v. Moore is verified, SCOTUS, and treatment.field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The treatment scope note says Moore remains controlling for probable-cause arrests that violate state arrest law and resulting incident searches.
All disclosed treatment edges are field_iii='mentioned', with no disclosed overruling/limitation of Moore's relevant point.
Shipley v. California is verified, SCOTUS, and treatment.field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The treatment scope note says Shipley applies the search-incident limits and has no negative treatment.
Disclosed progeny edges are only field_iii='mentioned'.
Vale v. Louisiana is verified, SCOTUS, and treatment.field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The treatment scope note says Vale still controls that a search incident to arrest cannot reach a house when the arrest occurs outside it.
No disclosed edge overrules, abrogates, or limits the relevant point.
Atwater v. City of Lago Vista is verified, SCOTUS, and treatment.field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The treatment scope note expressly preserves the fine-only/very-minor-offense custodial-arrest rule and notes extension by Moore.
All disclosed treatment edges are only field_iii='mentioned'.
The lake record verifies the input case Peters v. New York as part of the consolidated Sibron v. New York opinion at 392 U.S. 40.
Treatment.field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The treatment scope note says the Peters point remains good law: where probable cause to arrest existed, the search was valid as incident to arrest.
residual_risks: The lake identity canonical_name_match is false because the canonical opinion is Sibron v. New York, though the record expressly tracks Peters as the input case.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Caption as Peters v. New York, decided with Sibron v. New York, when space permits.

reasons: Preston v. United States is verified, SCOTUS, and treatment.field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The treatment scope note says the SITA remoteness holding remains controlling.
The disclosed automobile-exception caveat distinguishes but does not overrule Preston's search-incident point.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep Preston phrased as a search-incident rule, not as a categorical bar on delayed vehicle searches under the automobile exception.

defect.evidence_quote: Frontier stub: treatment/progeny intentionally not derived until S6 promotion.
defect.problem: The page makes a treatment call that Trupiano was rejected and superseded/dead-letter, but the disclosed lake record does not verify Trupiano's treatment or progeny.
defect.proposed_fix: Do not use Trupiano for a current treatment proposition until the authority is promoted with derived treatment/progeny, or supply disclosed Rabinowitz/Chimel treatment records that verify the rejection/supersession point.

reasons: Trupiano's treatment.field_i_validity is unverified, not good_law/caution/overruled/limited.
The lake record has no treatment edges and no as_of_treatment date.
Under the ground rules, uncertainty from the disclosed record must be refuted rather than inferred.
residual_risks: The historical proposition may be true, but it is not verifiable from the disclosed Trupiano record.

defect.evidence_quote: Chadwick's core (property reduced to exclusive police control, no exigency, needs a warrant) survives outside the auto-container setting.
defect.problem: Chadwick is still live only with an important treatment caveat; the page should not present it without flagging the Acevedo automobile-container limitation.
defect.proposed_fix: Modify the Chadwick row to say the exclusive-police-control/no-exigency point survives outside the automobile-container context, but Chadwick is caution/limited by California v. Acevedo in that context.

reasons: United States v. Chadwick has treatment.field_i_validity caution, varies_by_point=true, as of 2026-06-30.
The point override identifies California v. Acevedo as limiting Chadwick.
The asserted exclusive-control SITA point matches the surviving core, so the assertion survives with the caveat.
residual_risks: Without the Acevedo caveat, readers may overread Chadwick in automobile-container scenarios.

reasons: United States v. Edwards is verified, SCOTUS, and treatment.field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The treatment scope note says Edwards remains controlling on timing: effects subject to search at arrest may be searched at jail after reasonable delay.
No disclosed treatment edge overrules or limits the relevant point.
Chimel v. California is verified, SCOTUS, and treatment.field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The treatment scope note describes Chimel as the foundational SITA rule and says its core is undisturbed.
Disclosed edges are only field_iii='mentioned'.
Hill v. California is verified, SCOTUS, and treatment.field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The treatment scope note preserves the reasonable good-faith wrong-person arrest and ensuing search-incident point.
No disclosed edge overrules, abrogates, or limits the relevant point.
Agnello v. United States is verified, SCOTUS, and treatment.field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The treatment scope note says the separate-home-away-from-arrest SITA limit survives and is consistent with Chimel.
All disclosed treatment edges are field_iii='mentioned'.
Go-Bart has treatment.field_i_validity good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The treatment scope note says the no-general-exploratory-search principle survives and was reaffirmed/structured in Chimel.
Disclosed treatment edges are only field_iii='mentioned'.
residual_risks: The lake status is under_review, but the disclosed treatment judgment is still good_law.

reasons: United States v. Robinson is verified, SCOTUS, and treatment.field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30.
No point override limits Robinson, and all disclosed treatment edges are field_iii='mentioned'.
The disclosed record therefore does not show any supersession, overruling, abrogation, or limitation of the full-search-of-person anchor.
residual_risks: The Robinson scope note is a migration note rather than a substantive treatment explanation, but the judgment field is good_law.

reasons: Cupp v. Murphy is verified, SCOTUS, and treatment.field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The treatment scope note confirms a narrow surviving rule for a very limited intrusion on probable cause to preserve readily destructible evidence without formal arrest.
No disclosed edge overrules or limits the relevant point.
Knowles v. Iowa is verified, SCOTUS, and treatment.field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The treatment scope note says Knowles is controlling and that there is no search incident to citation.
All disclosed treatment edges are field_iii='mentioned'.
Lens B only: the black-letter proposition cites Robinson and Chimel, both verified SCOTUS records with treatment.field_i_validity good_law as of 2026-06-30.
Chimel's treatment scope note says the foundational SITA rule remains undisturbed.
Robinson has no point override and no disclosed non-mentioned negative treatment edge.
residual_risks: No support or quote-fidelity finding made under this lens.
